newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's BES boosts first-half profit.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's BES boosts first-half profit.

text.p: Portuguese bank Banco Espirito Santo said on Tuesday it boosted consolidated net profit by 43 percent to 15.2 billion escudos ($83.8 million) in the first six months, compared to the same year-ago period, after raising market share and margins.

"Besides an improvement in the national economy, which permitted strong growth in overall activity, the financial result was due essentially to an increase in market share, a more adequate mix of products, and the growth of margins of some subsidiaries," a statement said.
It said it expected the rate of growth of consolidated profits to slow down in the second half of 1997 as some markets would not grow as quickly as in the first half.
BES said operating costs rose by 15.3 percent to 42.2 billion escudos, partly due to the strong growth of some subsidiaries.

The ratio of operating costs to net assets fell to 2.19 percent at end-June 1997, down from 2.40 percent at end-June 1996, BES said. The ratio of operating costs to total assets stood at 1.76 percent at end-June 1997, compared with 2.00 percent at end-June 1996.
"The ratios fell as a result of rationalisation efforts," BES said.
Consolidated net assets stood at 3.846 trillion escudos at end-June 1997, up from 3.054 trillion. Loans stood at 1.739 trillion escudos, up from 1.354 trillion.
The ratio of bad loans to total consolidated loans fell to 3.01 percent at end-June 1997 from 4.05 percent at end-June 1996.
